findings.description: No action required. The 11 rejection sub-cases assert only that decoding returns an error plus whole-struct receiver preservation, not which guard rejected. Two sub-cases are not uniquely attributable: 'missing commit' and 'missing tree digest' would still fail through Subject.Validate() if decodeStrictObject's required-field check were removed, because the zero value fails validateGitObjectID/validateSHA256. The frozen outcome required preservation on rejection and full replacement on success (not error identity). The sub-cases that pin a guard are the duplicate member (RejectDuplicateJSONMembers), the unknown field (DisallowUnknownFields) and the three semantic validators. They do not pin the object-shape check, the required-field check or the trailing-data guard: a non-object or field-missing input is already rejected by encoding/json type errors and Subject.Validate(), and no input carries trailing data for ensureDecoderEOF to reject, so removing those checks is not observable through this test.

explanations.Explain why assigning the decoded Subjec: Subject.UnmarshalJSON (daemon/internal/protocol/goal_subject.go:51-62) decodes into a function-local subjectWire, converts it into a local Subject, runs value.Validate(), and only then executes the single statement *subject = value. Every failure return precedes that one assignment: decodeStrictObject rejects empty/whitespace input and non-object values, rejects duplicate members through RejectDuplicateJSONMembers, rejects a missing required field, rejects unknown fields through decoder.DisallowUnknownFields plus json type errors, and rejects trailing data through ensureDecoderEOF; value.Validate() then rejects a bad resource_id, commit or tree_digest. No code path assigns subject.ResourceID, subject.Commit or subject.TreeDigest individually, so the receiver cannot be half-updated: it changes atomically from the caller's previous bytes to a fully validated value, or it does not change at all. Decoding straight into the receiver (json.Unmarshal(data, subject)) would write field by field, and Go's encoding/json keeps assigning later members after an earlier member error, so a caller could observe a partially mutated Subject even though the call returned an error. Sealed evidence: protocol-tests stdout sha256:58107cf6... with validator stdout sha256:17ef5047... printing 'verified TestSubjectUnmarshalPreservesReceiverOnFailure: run=1 pass=1 skip=0' and the same line for TestSubjectUnmarshalReplacesReceiverOnSuccess (assert-go-test-json.py requires run=1, pass=1, skip=0, no skipped descendants), inside attempt-0001 sha256:38ad6dee..., bound to subject sha256:b14e8469....
explanations.Explain which malformed, incomplete or u: TestSubjectUnmarshalPreservesReceiverOnFailure applies 11 rejected inputs through json.Unmarshal into a receiver pre-populated with the shared identity testUUID/testCommit/testTreeDigest and asserts receiver == original after each rejection (whole-struct equality covers all three fields and any future field): empty input; array instead of object; truncated object (syntax error); non-string tree_digest (true); missing commit; missing tree_digest; unknown field 'unexpected'; duplicated resource_id member; invalid resource_id 'not-a-uuid'; invalid commit 'abc123'; invalid tree_digest 'sha256:zzzz'. Nine of the eleven reach Subject.UnmarshalJSON: the empty and truncated inputs are rejected by encoding/json's own syntax check before the custom method is called. Within the custom method they exercise the JSON type error, each required-field absence, the unknown-field rejection, the duplicate-member rejection and each of the three semantic validators. They do not pin the object-shape check (a non-object input already fails as a JSON type error) or the trailing-data guard (no input carries trailing data), so removing either check would not change this test's outcome. TestSubjectUnmarshalReplacesReceiverOnSuccess supplies a fully valid document whose every value differs from the pre-existing identity (22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222 vs 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111; fedcba98... vs 01234567...; sha256:0000... vs sha256:0123...) and asserts receiver == replacement plus explicit per-field inequality against the original. A receiver that was never written would still hold the original identity and fail that assertion, so preservation on failure is demonstrated as conditional validated-then-assigned behavior, not as an inert decoder that ignores every input. The file is a new, explicitly scoped test; daemon/internal/protocol/goal_subject.go and every baseline Go test are unmodified in this revision.
